Check the rider’s actual position before crossing the lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01"]},{"text":"The source distinguishes bicycle visibility from motorcycle lighting. A driver still needs to look for the bicycle rather than assume a lamp makes it obvious.","fact_ids":["sec08-F02"]},{"text":"The warning is about a possible lack of training. It supports extra caution rather than a guarantee about how a child will behave.","fact_ids":["sec08-F03"]},{"text":"The source connects startling behavior with crash risk. Respectful sharing is different from using noise or vehicle movement to pressure a rider.","fact_ids":["sec08-F04"]},{"text":"The nighttime front requirement is a white light. Other visibility equipment does not replace that specified front-light function.","fact_ids":["sec08-F05"]},{"text":"The source keeps required reflectors and an optional added lamp in different categories. Choosing one does not erase another equipment requirement.","fact_ids":["sec08-F06"]},{"text":"The source permits alternative reflection types while retaining both-wheel and visibility conditions for the stated arrangement.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07"]},{"text":"The source specifies the conditions for its brake-strength standard. The surface conditions are part of the equipment description rather than an interchangeable test setting.","fact_ids":["sec08-F08"]},{"text":"The flag is encouraged for visibility from behind. A recommendation is not a replacement for the separately required equipment or a guarantee of detection.","fact_ids":["sec08-F09"]},{"text":"The source names several places where bicycle movement may develop. Vehicle status does not mean every movement will already be obvious or signaled.","fact_ids":["sec08-F10"]},{"text":"Parking still concerns approaching traffic. Being stationary does not replace clearance of travel lanes or two-direction visibility.","fact_ids":["sec08-F11"]},{"text":"The source combines placement, brake use and the appropriate transmission setting. One component should not be treated as replacing all the others.","fact_ids":["sec08-F12"]},{"text":"Opening a door affects the surrounding traffic space. The source pairs a traffic check with curbside exit when possible and prompt closing.","fact_ids":["sec08-F13"]},{"text":"The instruction is not limited to a long absence or unfamiliar location. Leaving the keys inside does not preserve the stated preparation.","fact_ids":["sec08-F14"]},{"text":"The source directs roadway parking away from traffic and toward the curb or shoulder edge, not into a travel lane.","fact_ids":["sec08-F15"]},{"text":"The distance concerns lateral placement beside the curb or shoulder. It should not be confused with another parking measurement.","fact_ids":["sec08-F16"]},{"text":"The front light, rear reflectors and optional added rear light have different roles in the source. Keep mandatory and additional equipment distinct.","fact_ids":["sec08-R01"]},{"text":"The reflector arrangement retains placement, color and visibility conditions. A front light does not make those conditions disappear.","fact_ids":["sec08-R02"]},{"text":"The turning decision depends on what the cyclist has actually done. An expectation about the proper passing side does not establish that the path is clear.","fact_ids":["sec08-R03"]},{"text":"Vehicle status and a rider’s training are different matters. The source warns that young untrained riders need extra caution.","fact_ids":["sec08-R04"]},{"text":"The conditions work together. Meeting one parking-position goal does not make the vehicle clear and visible in every other respect.","fact_ids":["sec08-R05"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"A learner faces this decision: Before turning right across a cyclist’s lane, what should the driver confirm?","fact_ids":["sec08-F01"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The proposed response is “That the rider must disappear from view.”. Before turning right across a cyclist in the lane, confirm the rider has yielded or passed, since bikes should pass left but often do not.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Check the cyclist’s actual position","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F10","sec08-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"An expected passing side does not prove that the turn path is clear.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F10","sec08-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before turning right across a cyclist’s lane, look at what the rider has actually done. The handbook says to confirm that the cyclist has yielded or passed, rather than assume the rider is on the expected passing side. It also tells motorists to treat bicycles as vehicles and watch for movement at entries, bikeways, sidewalks, turns and between parked cars. A signal communicates the driver’s intention but does not establish that the bicycle is clear. Keep the actual path and the rider’s position in the turning decision instead of relying on what another road user should do.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F10","sec08-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Look carefully and avoid pressure","fact_ids":["sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A rider’s limited training calls for caution rather than startling behavior.","fact_ids":["sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-R04"]},{"text":"Bicycle awareness should not depend on a rider being conspicuous or formally trained.","fact_ids":["sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Bicycle awareness should not depend on a rider being conspicuous or formally trained. The handbook says bicycles can be difficult to see and distinguishes their daytime lighting from motorcycles. It calls for extra caution with young riders who may not have been trained or tested. It also warns against honking, shouting or swerving at cyclists in a way that startles them. These points work together: look carefully, allow for an unexpected movement and share space respectfully. Pressuring a less predictable rider does not make the situation more controlled.","fact_ids":["sec08-F02","sec08-F03","sec08-F04","sec08-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Separate required and added lighting","fact_ids":["sec08-F05","sec08-F06","sec08-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"An optional rear lamp does not remove the mandatory equipment.","fact_ids":["sec08-F05","sec08-F06","sec08-R01"]},{"text":"Night bicycle visibility has mandatory and additional equipment in the source.","fact_ids":["sec08-F05","sec08-F06","sec08-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Night bicycle visibility has mandatory and additional equipment in the source. The handbook requires a white front light with the stated visibility and rear reflectors, while a red rear light is an optional addition. Keep those categories distinct. Adding a rear lamp does not turn the front light into an option, and not choosing the extra lamp does not make the rear reflectors optional. This is why remembering only that a bicycle has some visible equipment is not enough to recover the source’s arrangement. Identify the front light, the required reflectors and any added rear light separately.","fact_ids":["sec08-F05","sec08-F06","sec08-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Keep each equipment condition","fact_ids":["sec08-F07","sec08-F08","sec08-F09","sec08-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"A recommended visibility aid does not substitute for required equipment.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07","sec08-F08","sec08-F09","sec08-R02"]},{"text":"The wheel-reflection arrangement also has conditions.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07","sec08-F08","sec08-F09","sec08-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"The wheel-reflection arrangement also has conditions. The source allows reflective sidewalls or the specified spoke reflectors on both wheels, retaining the placement near the rim, the color options and visibility from both sides. It separately describes a bicycle-brake strength standard on dry, level, clean pavement and encourages a fluorescent orange flag for visibility from behind. These are different equipment points. A recommended flag is not a substitute for required lighting or reflectors, and a brake standard’s stated surface should not be replaced with an arbitrary test setting.","fact_ids":["sec08-F07","sec08-F08","sec08-F09","sec08-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"A parked vehicle still affects traffic","fact_ids":["sec08-F11","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Edge placement does not replace lane clearance or visibility.","fact_ids":["sec08-F11","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-R05"]},{"text":"Parking position affects the traffic that continues around the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec08-F11","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Parking position affects the traffic that continues around the vehicle. The handbook says to stay clear of travel lanes, remain visible to approaching traffic from both directions and, on a roadway, place the vehicle as far from traffic as possible near the curb or shoulder edge. It also gives a lateral distance limit for that position. Keep visibility, lane clearance and edge placement together. A stationary vehicle can still be an obstruction, and being close to an edge does not establish that approaching traffic from both directions has a clear view of it.","fact_ids":["sec08-F11","sec08-F15","sec08-F16","sec08-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Prepare the vehicle and the exit","fact_ids":["sec08-F12","sec08-F13","sec08-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Door checks remain separate from brake, transmission and security steps.","fact_ids":["sec08-F12","sec08-F13","sec08-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Once a parking place is chosen, preparation includes the vehicle’s settings and the people leaving it. Use marked areas, set the brake and put a manual in gear or an automatic in park as described. Check traffic before opening doors, use the curbside exit when possible and close doors promptly. Take the keys and lock the vehicle when leaving. These steps address different risks; a correct transmission setting does not show that a door can be opened safely, and a short intended stop does not remove the source’s key-and-lock instruction.","fact_ids":["sec08-F12","sec08-F13","sec08-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check before crossing the bicycle path","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F03","sec08-F10","sec08-R03","sec08-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A signal and an expectation do not establish the rider’s position.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F03","sec08-F10","sec08-R03","sec08-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"A driver signals a right turn and assumes that every cyclist must already have passed on the left. What needs correcting? The handbook warns that actual bicycle passing behavior may differ, so the driver checks that the rider has yielded or passed before crossing the lane. The vehicle status of a bicycle and the possible inexperience of a young rider both remain relevant. A rule about the expected side does not tell the driver where this rider is now. The safe decision uses the actual position rather than treating an expectation or a signal as proof that the path is clear.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F03","sec08-F10","sec08-R03","sec08-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u01-slide-8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Check the space when using it","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F04","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F13","sec08-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"An earlier observation does not replace the check for the current movement.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F04","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F13","sec08-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Use the surrounding-space check to connect these topics without merging their rules. When moving near bicycles, look for the actual rider and avoid behavior that may startle them. When parking, clear the travel lane and remain visible while positioning near the appropriate edge. When opening a door, check the traffic space that the door will enter. These actions all concern how the vehicle affects others, but one successful check does not answer the rest. Spotting a bicycle earlier is not the same as checking its position at the turn or checking for traffic before opening the door.","fact_ids":["sec08-F01","sec08-F04","sec08-F10","sec08-F11","sec08-F13","sec08-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec08-u02","module_id":"sec08-m02","objective_ids":["sec08-F17-understand","sec08-F18-understand","sec08-F19-understand","sec08-F20-understand","sec08-F21-understand","sec08-R06-understand","sec08-R07-understand","sec08-R08-understand","sec08-R09-understand"],"title":{"text":"Parallel and hill parking","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21","sec08-R06","sec08-R07","sec08-R08","sec08-R09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The night-parking provision combines fore-and-aft visibility with dimmed headlights. Backing adds a specific double-check for smaller or less obvious road users.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18"]},{"text":"The setup establishes a starting position before the steering sequence. Signal when leaving a space, scanning both ways and double-checking for vehicles, bikes and pedestrians when backing out.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-slide-1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Night parking retains a lighting condition","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stopping the engine does not answer the night-parking visibility requirement.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Night parking on a roadway or shoulder has a lighting arrangement in the handbook: visible front and rear lights with headlights dimmed. Keep that rule separate from the act of switching off the engine or selecting a transmission position. The vehicle is still part of the traffic environment after it stops. The source’s daytime comparison does not turn the nighttime arrangement into an option, nor does using lights create permission to block a travel lane. Learn the lighting condition as an addition to the ordinary choice of a suitable parking position, not as a substitute for it.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-slide-2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Look at the current space","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"A signal announces intention; it does not confirm a clear backing path.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]},{"text":"Leaving a space reverses the attention outward again.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Leaving a space reverses the attention outward again. The handbook calls for signaling and scanning both ways and adds a double-check for vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians when backing out. A signal is information for others, not proof that they have seen it or granted a gap. A glance made before entering the vehicle may also be out of date by the time reversing begins. The useful distinction is between announcing an intention and confirming the actual surrounding space. Preserve both, especially where smaller road users can be less obvious behind or beside parked vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-slide-3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Connect setup and sequence","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"The steering sequence starts from the described alignment.","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-R09"]},{"text":"Parallel parking begins with a setup before the steering sequence.","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Parallel parking begins with a setup before the steering sequence. The handbook describes a signal and alignment beside the lead vehicle with the stated lateral spacing and even rear bumpers. It then describes backing with a right cut, a later left swing into the space and forward straightening. Keep the starting position with the sequence instead of treating each steering direction as a disconnected instruction. A random starting gap changes the maneuver being attempted, while keeping one steering lock throughout leaves out the source’s later change and straightening step.","fact_ids":["sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-slide-4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Use slope and curb presence","fact_ids":["sec08-F21","sec08-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"One wheel direction is not the answer for every hill.","fact_ids":["sec08-F21","sec08-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Hill parking adds a choice about where the wheels direct a possible rollaway. In the source, downhill with a curb turns toward it, uphill with a curb turns away, and the curb-free uphill situation aims away from the street. The purpose stated is to keep a rollaway from entering traffic. Keep slope and curb presence in the decision rather than memorize one direction for every hill. A curb-free case cannot be answered as if the curb were still there, and a favorable wheel direction does not replace the separate parking-brake and transmission preparation described elsewhere.","fact_ids":["sec08-F21","sec08-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-slide-5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the full backing environment","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Include bicycles and pedestrians rather than only large vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"A driver signals before backing out but checks only for large vehicles. What part of the handbook’s preparation is missing? The source calls for scanning both ways and a double-check for vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians. The signal does not guarantee that those people have noticed the planned movement, and an earlier empty space does not prove the current path is still clear. This example tests the actual observation before and during departure from the space. A correctly performed parking maneuver earlier does not make the later exit safe without its own check.","fact_ids":["sec08-F18","sec08-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec08-u02-slide-6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Keep the parking stages distinct","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21","sec08-R06","sec08-R07","sec08-R08","sec08-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"A successful arrival does not perform the later departure check.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21","sec08-R06","sec08-R07","sec08-R08","sec08-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"For recall, separate arriving, securing and leaving. Parallel parking has its described alignment and steering order. Hill parking keeps the wheel direction with slope and curb presence. Night parking retains its fore-and-aft lighting arrangement. Leaving the space requires a signal and current observation, with the extra backing check for bicycles and pedestrians. These are connected parts of using a parking place, but they do different jobs. A driver should not use success at one stage as evidence that every later stage has already been checked or that a changed situation needs no new observation.","fact_ids":["sec08-F17","sec08-F18","sec08-F19","sec08-F20","sec08-F21","sec08-R06","sec08-R07","sec08-R08","sec08-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec08-u03","module_id":"sec08-m03","objective_ids":["sec08-F22-understand","sec08-F23-understand","sec08-F24-understand","sec08-F25-understand","sec08-F26-understand","sec08-F27-understand","sec08-F28-understand","sec08-F29-understand","sec08-F30-understand","sec08-R10-understand","sec08-R11-understand","sec08-R12-understand"],"title":{"text":"Prohibited parking","fact_ids":["sec08-F22","sec08-F23","sec08-F24","sec08-F25","sec08-F26","sec08-F27","sec08-F28","sec08-F29","sec08-F30","sec08-R10","sec08-R11","sec08-R12"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Each color has a stated purpose or prohibition.
